text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--There is no lack of foreign buyers for Danish businesses, the problem is to facilitate contact between potential buyers and sellers, economist Niels Dahl-Soerensen says.

--The Danish Road Haulage Association says that the government's new ecological package could harm the environment more than helps as it decreases the differential between the price of ultra-light diesel and other, less clean, fuels.

--Revenue from earlier environmental levies has been far below government forecasts but the ruling Social Democrats say that the measures are working, in that use of water and plastic bags has fallen.

--Tax Minister Carsten Koch plans to introduce an extra 25 percent levy on postal charges for mail order purchases. Danish mail order companies fear that the increase will drive many customers back to conventional shops or to postal shopping rivals in neighbouring Germany.

--Danish exports are picking up again after a period of stagnation, the Confederation of Danish Industries says.It cites a two percent rise in exports in the first quarter of 1997 compared to last year, but warns against expectations of a sudden boom.
--Den Danske Bank and Unidanmark pay almost the lowest dividends in Europe and risk being punished by international investors.
--Although telecommunications deregulation has given a tremendous boost to the Danish electronics industry, gains could be hit by a global shortage of components and a local lack of skilled workers.
